offence_severity: 302 IPC: Death (minimum 10 years to life imprisonment or death), 307 IPC: Attempted murder (minimum 10 years to life imprisonment or death)
physical_harm: Deceased suffered multiple severe injuries including incised wounds, chop wounds, fractures, and amputations, leading to death due to hemorrhage and shock.
number_of_offences: 34 counts charged; 8 accused convicted by trial court, 6 convictions confirmed, 2 acquitted
key_evidence_accepted: The testimony of PW-12 was natural and devoid of any exaggeration and the same is corroborated by the recovery of weapons of offence at the instance of the accused, medical evidence and other material on record.
witness_credibility: The deposition of PW12 is devoid of any exaggeration, completely trustworthy and reliable. Her evidence is reliable, should not leave any doubt in the mind of the Court and has to be corroborated by other evidence produced by the prosecution.
trial_duration: Trial court convicted 8 respondents, High Court acquitted them, Supreme Court confirmed conviction of 6 and acquitted 2
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Shankar Chillarge, Sonia Shankar Chillarge, Niruddha P. Mayee; Counsel for the State: Meenakshi Arora, Mahima, Anjani Kumar Jha, Vinay Naware, Dr. R.R. Deshpande, Yuvraj Gaikwad
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Convicted 8 accused, acquitted others; High Court: Acquitted respondents disbelieving PW-12; Supreme Court: Partly allowed appeal, confirmed conviction of 6, acquitted 2
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the sole eye-witness PW-12's testimony was natural, reliable, and corroborated by the recovery of weapons, medical evidence, and other material on record. The case against six accused was completely proved based on her testimony.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the testimony of PW-12 was not reliable and that the High Court should have acquitted the accused, as the prosecution failed to establish the common object of the unlawful assembly and the specific roles of the accused.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that a conviction can be founded on the testimony of a sole witness if it is reliable and corroborated by other evidence, and that the existence of a common object can be determined from the attending facts and circumstances.
precedent_relied_upon: State of U.P. v. Kishan Pal, Mohd Aslam v. State of Maharashtra, Anter Singh v. State of Rajasthan, Amerika Rai v. State of Bihar, Masalti v. State of U.P., and others.
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed because the prosecution case against six accused stood completely proved, and their roles in the assault and death of Tanaji were established through the testimony of PW-12 and corroborating evidence.
